sections.h2: Who values and bills a house in Midland?
sections.html:
In Midland County one office does both jobs: the Midland Central Appraisal District puts a value on each parcel and also mails the statements. The district works from 4631 Andrews Hwy and answers at 432-699-4991 on weekdays between 8 and 5.

Its news page records that roughly 548,842 statements for the 2026 tax year went into the mail on October 23, 2026. A parcel that lies in Martin County rather than Midland County belongs to a different appraisal and billing office, so call the Martin County tax office if that is your situation.

The district's FAQ lays out who does what. The appraisal district sets value, the Appraisal Review Board settles disagreements, the taxing units (city, school, county, college, hospital) choose budgets and rates, and a collector turns those into a bill and passes the money along.

sections.h2: How did Midland's rates change from 2025 to 2026?
sections.html:
The City of Midland moved from $0.347999 per $100 in 2025 to $0.383092 in 2026, a rise the appraisal district's rate page records alongside increases for the county, the college and the hospital. Midland ISD stayed flat at 0.841500.

sections.h2: What does Midland charge after the January 31 cutoff?
sections.html:
Statements are payable when they arrive, and the district says collection starts about October 1 and charges begin on February 1. The Comptroller puts numbers on it: 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest at the start of February, with the penalty gaining a point each month to a ceiling of 12 percent in July and interest continuing at a point a month.

  • An attorney's fee of up to 20 percent can be layered on top.
  • Older and disabled owners have a four-installment option.
  • Some collectors permit up to 36 months of instalments on a delinquent account, and only a residence homestead is guaranteed one.
  • To seek a waiver of the penalty and interest, apply in writing before day 181 after delinquency, and pay the tax within 21 days of learning it was late.

When you pay in person, bring the account number from your statement and keep the receipt with your closing papers if you are selling. Ask the district which payment types it accepts at the counter before you go.

sections.h2: Which exemptions does a Midland homestead get?
sections.html:
The district's exemption table shows Midland ISD taking $140,000 off a homestead, and no general homestead amount for the City of Midland. The city does help older owners, at $8,000 for age 65 or older.

  • Age 65 or older: county $150,000, city $8,000, hospital $20,000, college $8,000, Midland ISD $60,000.
  • Disability: county $150,000 and Midland ISD $60,000.
  • Only one of the age and disability exemptions can be claimed, and the district notes the age one is the better choice.
  • The county's optional homestead percentage is listed as 3 percent with a $5,000 minimum, with $0 granted in the table.
  • Veterans receive $5,000, $7,500, $10,000 or $12,000 by disability bracket, and 100 percent covers the full homesteadable value.

These exemptions follow whoever owned on January 1, so a buyer from later in the year files a new application. A late homestead filing is accepted up to a year after the tax goes delinquent. An owner turning 65 can apply any time in the birthday year and receive the exemption for that whole year.

sections.h2: When and how can I challenge a Midland value?
sections.html:
Notices of appraised value normally land in mid-April, per the district, and protests are due by May 15 or 30 days after the notice arrives, whichever is later. The Comptroller's calendar aims homestead notices at April 1, so start watching the mailbox early.

The district's FAQ says the notice describes the property, shows its value and exemptions, and estimates the tax. Values shift when comparable sales move or when a record is corrected for a measurement or a pool, so read the description line by line before you protest.

After the board rules, an unhappy owner may take the matter to district court or binding arbitration, or to the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the board value exceeds $1,000,000. The district reappraises every property at least every three years, and a qualified homestead's value cannot rise more than 10 percent a year, starting the year after the first exemption.

Census QuickFacts shows a city that added residents quickly this decade:

  • Population: 147,615 in the July 2025 estimate, up 11.1 percent from the 2020 estimates base. The 2020 census counted 132,524 and the 2010 census 111,147.
  • Area: 75.45 square miles of land, or 1,756.4 residents a mile in 2020.
  • Ownership: 65.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied (2020-2024), with a midpoint value of $319,200.
  • Monthly costs: $2,205 for owners with a mortgage, $766 without one, and $1,434 for renters.
  • Income: $89,585 for the median household, with 53,414 households in total.
  • Age: 10.1 percent of residents are 65 or older.

Those figures cover the whole city. Individual streets can run well above or below them, which is why the appraisal district's own record for your parcel matters more than any average.

sections.h2: What should a Midland seller do about property tax?
sections.html:
Pull your account from the appraisal district before listing, because the same office values the house and sends the bill. The tax lien attaches each January 1, so the owner on that date is on the hook for that year even if the deed changes hands soon after.

  • Ask the title company how that year's tax is being split with the buyer.
  • Tell the buyer to file a homestead application of their own, since the exemption on file belongs to the January 1 owner.
  • On a delinquent account, request a payoff that lists penalty, interest and any attorney fee.
  • For an inherited house, heirs not named on a recorded deed give the district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim the exemption.

Because Midland's rates rose between 2025 and 2026 while the school rate held steady, a buyer comparing your 2026 statement with an older one will see a higher city share. Keep both years' statements handy, and point the buyer to the district's rate page so the numbers come from the source.

faqs.q: What is Midland's city tax rate this cycle?
faqs.a: The 2026 tax year rate is $0.383092 per $100 of taxable value for the City of Midland, up from $0.347999 in 2025, according to the appraisal district. The school, county, college and hospital rates add to it.

faqs.q: Who sends Midland County tax statements?
faqs.a: The Midland Central Appraisal District mails them, and you can reach it at 4631 Andrews Hwy or 432-699-4991. For a Martin County parcel, ask the Martin County tax office.

faqs.q: Does the City of Midland grant a regular homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Not according to the district's table, which lists only $8,000 for owners 65 or older at the city level. Midland ISD gives $140,000 on a homestead.

faqs.q: Is it too late to claim a homestead exemption I forgot?
faqs.a: Possibly not. The district says a late application is accepted up to one year after the taxes become delinquent, and you have to file it yourself.

faqs.q: What does missing the January 31 date cost in Midland?
faqs.a: The Comptroller lists a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest from February 1, with the penalty reaching 12 percent in July and interest continuing monthly. An attorney fee up to 20 percent may follow.
